source_reviews.independent_solution: The incident ray, reflected ray and local normal are coplanar. At nonnormal incidence the ray arms lie on opposite sides of the normal. Incidence and reflection angles are measured from the normal and are equal; normal incidence gives two zero angles and retracing. The surface-referenced angles are complementary, not the named incidence/reflection angles.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Paraxial axis-parallel rays reflected by a concave mirror actually meet at the real principal focus in front. Convex reflected rays diverge, with backward extensions meeting at the virtual principal focus behind. The focus is not the curvature center: its paraxial distance from the vertex is R/2 rather than R.
